passage:
A dry village installed a water machine in the central square. Families could use a card to buy clean water at a low price.
Some people were unhappy. They said water should not come from a machine. Others said the machine was better than walking far to unsafe wells.
A local group helped older residents learn how to use the cards. They also made sure families without money could receive free water support.
The machine did not solve every water problem, but it made daily life safer.
The village learned that a tool is only fair when the system around it is fair too. Clean water requires both technology and care for people.
